design_detail: ACOG Clinical Practice Guideline No. 4 (screening and diagnosis); a priori protocol, librarian literature search, modified GRADE evidence-to-decision framework
population: Pregnant or postpartum individuals with mental health conditions
sample_size_detail: Guideline; no sample size
rationale: PubMed type Practice Guideline; abstract describes a clinical practice guideline with graded recommendations and Good Practice Points.

design_detail: Diagnostic manual (DSM-5-TR), American Psychiatric Association, 2022
population: Not applicable (psychiatric diagnostic criteria, general population)
sample_size_detail: Resource; no sample size
rationale: Citation is the DSM-5-TR; protocol lists diagnostic manuals under 'Not a study (resource)'. No abstract in file.

design_detail: Descriptive screening study (authors: 'sequential case series'); telephone EPDS screening at 4-6 weeks postpartum at one urban academic hospital, followed by SCID diagnostic home visits for screen-positive women; descriptive statistics and chi-square/Fisher tests only
severity_measure: Not applicable: descriptive prevalence/diagnostic yield study with no treatment or exposure comparison; no adjusted analyses
comparison_group: None for main aims (screen-positive vs screen-negative women compared descriptively on demographics)
population: Postpartum women delivering at Magee-Womens Hospital, Pittsburgh, screened 4-6 weeks postpartum
sample_size_detail: 17,426 eligible; 13,442 contacted; 10,000 screened; 1,396 screen-positive (EPDS>=10); 826 completed SCID home visits; 147 telephone MDD interviews
rationale: Purely descriptive screening/prevalence analysis (onset timing, self-harm ideation, diagnoses) with crude tests only. Self-labelled a case series, but it is a defined screened population rather than exposed cases, so coded as descriptive observational.

design_detail: Website: Alliance for Innovation on Maternal Health page on perinatal mental health conditions (saferbirth.org)
population: Not applicable (web resource on perinatal mental health conditions)
sample_size_detail: Resource; no sample size
rationale: File contains only a website citation with access date and no abstract; coded as a web resource. Could alternatively be viewed as a consensus practice bundle, but the file does not describe its content.

design_detail: Narrative clinical review of postpartum psychosis (epidemiology, etiology, diagnosis, treatment, prevention)
population: Women with postpartum psychosis/mania
sample_size_detail: Narrative review; no pooled sample
rationale: Authors 'reviewed' and 'synthesized' literature with no systematic search, eligibility criteria, or pooling described; PubMed type Review.

design_detail: USPSTF recommendation statement on depression screening in adults (B recommendation), based on evidence review
population: Adults aged 18+, including older adults and pregnant and postpartum women
sample_size_detail: Recommendation statement; no sample size
rationale: Explicitly a USPSTF 'Recommendation Statement'; PubMed type Practice Guideline.

design_detail: American Academy of Pediatrics committee clinical report with practice and advocacy recommendations on perinatal depression in pediatric practice
population: Mothers with perinatal depression and their infants seen in pediatric medical homes
sample_size_detail: Guidance document; no sample size
rationale: Authored on behalf of an AAP committee and the abstract issues recommendations (e.g., PPD screening at 1-, 2-, 4-, 6-month visits). PubMed labels it a Review, so narrative review is a plausible alternative.

design_detail: American College of Nurse-Midwives position statement on mental health during childbirth and across the lifespan (web PDF)
population: Women during childbirth and across the lifespan
sample_size_detail: Position statement; no sample size
rationale: Citation identifies the document as a 'Position statement'; protocol places position statements under Guideline/consensus statement. No abstract in file.

design_detail: Training program website: National Curriculum in Reproductive Psychiatry (ncrptraining.org)
population: Not applicable (clinician education resource in reproductive psychiatry)
sample_size_detail: Resource; no sample size
rationale: Citation is a curriculum/training website; protocol lists training programs under 'Not a study (resource)'.

design_detail: Systematic literature search (MEDLINE, PreMEDLINE, Current Contents, Biological Abstracts, PsycINFO 1966-2002) with pooled analysis of maternal plasma, breast milk and infant plasma antidepressant levels
comparison_group: None (infant levels standardized to average maternal levels; comparisons across drugs)
population: Lactating mothers taking antidepressants and their nursing infants
sample_size_detail: 67 relevant studies identified, 57 included; total pooled mother-infant pairs not reported in abstract
rationale: A 'pooled analysis' of 57 drug-level studies identified by systematic search; protocol places pooled analyses of multiple studies under code 7, ahead of PK. Component studies are drug-level reports including case reports (non-randomized).

design_detail: Narrative review and commentary on US suicide disparities, illustrated with CDC WONDER mortality data (1999-2019)
population: US population (suicide deaths, all ages)
sample_size_detail: Narrative review; descriptive presentation of national mortality data, no analytic sample
rationale: Authors state 'this is not a systematic review' and describe it as part narrative review, part commentary; no perinatal focus.

design_detail: Meta-analysis of double-blind placebo-controlled antidepressant relapse-prevention trials identified by systematic literature search; pooled ORs (RevMan 5)
population: Adults with depressive disorders who responded to acute antidepressant treatment
sample_size_detail: 54 double-blind placebo-controlled relapse prevention studies, patient n = 9268
rationale: Explicit meta-analysis of 54 double-blind placebo-controlled RCTs with 9268 patients; not a perinatal population.

design_detail: Prospective cohort (Yale pregnancy cohort, 137 obstetric practices/clinics, CT and western MA, 2005-2009); Cox regression with time-dependent, 2-month-lagged antidepressant use; CIDI-assessed major depressive episode
severity_measure: Number of prior lifetime depressive episodes (1, 2, 3, 4+), number of psychiatric hospitalizations for depression, age at first episode (<14 etc.), and MDE in 6 months before pregnancy
comparison_group: Pregnant women with a history of depression not using antidepressants (time-varying)
population: Pregnant women with a history of depressive disorder recruited <17 weeks gestation, Connecticut and western Massachusetts, 2005-2009, followed to 2 months postpartum
sample_size_detail: Analytic sample 778 women with prior depression (from 2,793 interviewed); 130 used antidepressants during study period; 617 completed both follow-up interviews; 123 developed an MDE
rationale: Non-randomized comparison adjusted for pre-selected covariates the authors call 'correlates of severe depressive illness': prior episodes, hospitalization, onset age, recent MDE (Table 2).

design_detail: Systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis (PRISMA; MEDLINE, CENTRAL, EMBASE, Scopus to Dec 2019) of psychotherapy vs conventional obstetric care for antenatal depression, anxiety and quality of life
population: Pregnant women in the antenatal period
sample_size_detail: 22 studies (17 RCTs, 5 non-randomized controlled clinical trials); 2146 pregnant women, 1180 in psychotherapy groups
rationale: PRISMA systematic review with meta-analysis; included 17 RCTs and 5 controlled clinical trials (non-randomized), so component designs are mixed.

design_detail: Joint APA-ACOG work group consensus report: non-systematic review of Medline/bibliography literature with iterative drafts to consensus and management algorithms for depression before and during pregnancy
population: Women with depression who are pregnant or planning pregnancy
sample_size_detail: Consensus report; no sample size
rationale: Representatives of APA and ACOG reviewed literature 'until consensus was achieved' and present management algorithms; coded as a consensus statement, though PubMed labels it a Review and narrative review is a defensible alternative.

design_detail: Clinical toolkit: Lifeline for Moms Perinatal Mental Health Toolkit, University of Massachusetts Medical School, 2019 (web)
population: Not applicable (clinician toolkit for perinatal mental health)
sample_size_detail: Resource; no sample size
rationale: Citation is an online clinical toolkit (source for ACOG Figures 1 and 2), not a study. No abstract in file.

design_detail: Cochrane systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs of TCAs or SSRIs vs placebo in primary care patients
population: Adults under 65 with depression recruited in primary care
sample_size_detail: 14 studies (16 comparisons); 1364 participants in intervention groups and 919 in placebo groups (sum 2283)
rationale: Cochrane review restricted to randomised controlled trials of antidepressant vs placebo; pooled N computed from reported arm totals.

design_detail: Rationale-and-design article for a pharmacokinetic investigation to optimize SSRI dosing in pregnant women with depression
population: Pregnant women with depression treated with SSRIs
sample_size_detail: Design paper; no results reported
rationale: Title states 'Rationale and design'; abstract presents background only, no results.

design_detail: Retrospective cohort, Quebec health administrative databases (deliveries 1998-2002); multivariable log-binomial regression, miscarriage risk corrected for induced abortion
severity_measure: Abstract-only; covariates in multivariable model not listed. Comparison groups defined by depression diagnosis (diagnosis alone does not count as severity)
comparison_group: Unexposed women without depression (reference); also depressed women without first-trimester antidepressants, and women on hypothyroid medication
population: Pregnant women in Quebec administrative databases, 1998-2002
sample_size_detail: 41,964 pregnant women identified; sizes of the exposed and comparison groups not reported in abstract
rationale: Non-randomized comparison with 'adjusted relative risk' from multivariable models, but covariate list unavailable; coded excl. severity by default with severity Unclear.

design_detail: Systematic review and meta-analysis (Embase, Medline, PsycINFO, CINAHL to Dec 2012) of antidepressant exposure and PPHN; random/fixed effects pooled ORs by exposure timing
comparison_group: Unexposed pregnant women (as defined in included studies)
population: Infants of pregnant women with and without antenatal antidepressant exposure
sample_size_detail: 7 studies (5 cohort, 2 case-control); total pooled participants not reported in text (supplementary table)
rationale: Explicit systematic review and meta-analysis; eligibility limited to cohort and case-control studies; seven included.

design_detail: Updated systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis (PubMed, Medline, EMBASE, Web of Science, Google Scholar, 1960-2017) of SSRI use in pregnancy and PPHN
comparison_group: Infants of mothers without SSRI use in pregnancy
population: Pregnant women and their newborns
sample_size_detail: 9 cohort and case-control studies with 7,540,265 subjects reviewed; 8 studies in the meta-analysis
rationale: Meta-analysis of 9 cohort and case-control studies with total subjects reported in abstract.

design_detail: Secondary analysis of two prospective observational cohort studies (Cleveland and Pittsburgh, 2000-2011); blinded Finnegan Scale exam at 2-4 weeks; chi-square comparisons plus multivariable logistic regression adjusting for preterm birth, maternal race and age
severity_measure: Adjusted model included only preterm birth, maternal race and age; SIGH-ADS depression scores were measured and compared across groups but not entered as covariates
comparison_group: Unexposed women without mood disorder (n=79) and women with untreated mood disorder (n=94)
population: Pregnant women with MDD or bipolar disorder and healthy comparison women, Cleveland OH and Pittsburgh PA, 2000-2011, and their infants
sample_size_detail: 214 mothers/infants: 41 SRI-exposed, 94 untreated mood disorder, 79 comparison
rationale: Main results are crude rates (chi-square), but the exposure comparison was also run with adjustment for preterm birth, race and age, so coded adjusted excl. severity. No depression-severity covariate in the model.

design_detail: Systematic review and meta-analysis (MEDLINE, EMBASE, CINAHL, PsycINFO to June 2010) of prenatal antidepressant exposure and poor neonatal adaptation syndrome, respiratory distress and tremors
comparison_group: Infants not exposed to antidepressants in utero
population: Infants of pregnant women with or without antidepressant exposure
sample_size_detail: 12 cohort and case-control studies included; pooled participants not reported in abstract
rationale: Explicit systematic review/meta-analysis restricted to cohort and case-control studies; 12 included.

design_detail: Systematic literature review (MEDLINE 1966-2005, PsycINFO, FDA advisory data) with explicit inclusion criteria and Mantel-Haenszel summary risk ratios for neonatal behavioral syndrome after late SRI exposure
population: Neonates with late in utero SRI exposure
sample_size_detail: 13 case reports (18 cases) and 9 cohort studies; total pooled participants not reported
rationale: Self-described literature review, but with systematic database searches, inclusion criteria and pooled Mantel-Haenszel risk ratio, so coded as systematic review/meta-analysis. Components are case reports and cohort studies.

design_detail: Population-based registry cohort, Swedish Medical Birth Register; infants of mothers reporting benzodiazepine/hypnotic BZD-receptor agonist use compared with all births; adjusted ORs
severity_measure: Abstract-only; adjusted OR reported but covariates not listed; no indication of anxiety/insomnia severity measures
comparison_group: All births in the Swedish Medical Birth Register (general population)
population: Infants born in Sweden recorded in the Medical Birth Register
sample_size_detail: 1979 infants (1944 mothers) exposed in early pregnancy and 401 infants (390 mothers) exposed in late pregnancy, compared with all births (n = 873,879)
rationale: Registry cohort with 'adjusted OR' for malformations, but covariates not available in the abstract; coded excl. severity by default with severity Unclear.

design_detail: ACOG Practice Bulletin No. 187 on neural tube defects (management recommendations)
population: Pregnancies complicated by fetal neural tube defects; women of reproductive age (prevention)
sample_size_detail: Practice bulletin; no sample size
rationale: Explicitly a Practice Bulletin; PubMed type Practice Guideline.

design_detail: Narrative review (Current Opinion in Cardiology) on high-dose periconceptional folic acid for preventing congenital heart defects, drawing on animal and clinical studies
population: Women planning pregnancy/early pregnancy and their offspring (with animal data)
sample_size_detail: Narrative review; no sample size
rationale: 'Purpose of Review' format with no systematic search or pooling; PubMed type Review.

design_detail: Pooled individual-level reanalysis of five prospective European cohort studies of antiepileptic drug exposure in pregnancy and major congenital malformations
severity_measure: Not applicable (pooled analysis); abstract mentions comparison with matched nonepileptic controls but no epilepsy-severity measures
comparison_group: Children of matched nonepileptic control pregnancies (n=158); also comparisons across AED regimens and VPA doses
population: Children of mothers with epilepsy exposed to AEDs in utero and unexposed control children, five European prospective studies
sample_size_detail: 1,221 AED-exposed children and 158 unexposed controls; main exposed-vs-control RR based on subgroup of 192 exposed vs 158 matched controls
rationale: Data from five prospective studies 'pooled and reanalyzed'; protocol lists pooled/IPD analyses of multiple studies under code 7 (PubMed type Meta-Analysis). Could alternatively be coded as an observational cohort analysis.

design_detail: Prospective pharmacokinetic study of carbamazepine and its epoxide/diol metabolites in maternal serum, urine and amniotic fluid in early pregnancy, by dose, comedication and pregnancy outcome
severity_measure: Not applicable (PK study; no confounder-adjusted clinical outcome comparison)
comparison_group: Pregnancies with normal vs malformed outcome; CBZ monotherapy vs comedication (drug-level comparisons only)
population: Pregnant women with epilepsy taking carbamazepine, referred before 16 weeks for prenatal diagnosis (Netherlands)
sample_size_detail: 100 pregnancies with first-trimester CBZ exposure, including 7 with malformed outcome
rationale: Primary measures are drug and metabolite concentrations across maternal serum, urine and amniotic fluid; outcome comparison is of drug levels only, unadjusted.

design_detail: Single case report of a neonate with fatal cardiac malformation attributed to maternal valproate
population: Neonate with prenatal valproate exposure
sample_size_detail: One neonate
rationale: PubMed type Case Reports; abstract presents a single neonate.

design_detail: Clinical case series evaluating fetal valproate syndrome phenotype in valproate-exposed children (monotherapy vs combination therapy described)
comparison_group: None (descriptive contrast of VPA monotherapy vs VPA plus other anticonvulsants)
population: Children exposed to valproic acid in utero
sample_size_detail: 19 VPA-exposed children evaluated
rationale: Describes 19 exposed children without an unexposed comparison group; PubMed type Case Reports.

design_detail: Case series of VPA-exposed infants from the Spanish Collaborative Study of Congenital Malformations (ECEMC, 1976-1988), combined with review of published cases and epidemiologic data
comparison_group: None (descriptive contrast of VPA monotherapy vs VPA plus other anticonvulsants)
population: Infants prenatally exposed to valproic acid, Spain, 1976-1988
sample_size_detail: 28 VPA-exposed patients: 15 monotherapy, 13 polytherapy
rationale: Primary content is clinical description of 28 exposed cases plus literature/epidemiologic synthesis, with no unexposed comparison group.

design_detail: Letter to the editor reporting case(s) of fetal valproate syndrome with autism (comment on Williams et al. 2001)
population: Child(ren) with prenatal valproate exposure
sample_size_detail: Number of cases not determinable; file has no abstract (metadata only)
rationale: PubMed types Case Reports; Comment; Letter, but no abstract is in the file, so content and case count cannot be verified.

design_detail: Case series of patients with fetal valproate syndrome and autism
population: Children with fetal valproate syndrome
sample_size_detail: Five additional patients (one previously reported patient not counted)
rationale: Abstract presents 'five additional patients' with FVS and autism without a comparison group.

design_detail: Retrospective cohort via postal questionnaire survey of women attending a UK regional epilepsy clinic; odds ratios of additional educational needs by in utero AED exposure
severity_measure: Abstract-only; ORs reported but never stated whether adjusted; no epilepsy severity or seizure-frequency measures mentioned (Amendment 1 rule b)
comparison_group: Children of mothers with epilepsy not exposed to AEDs in utero (n=176)
population: School-age children (4-18) of women aged 16-40 with epilepsy registered at the Mersey Regional Epilepsy Clinic, UK
sample_size_detail: 1267 women approached, 721 responded, 330 with live births; 594 children, 400 of school age (150 monotherapy, 74 polytherapy, 176 unexposed)
rationale: Questionnaire-based retrospective comparison of exposed vs unexposed children with ORs; abstract never says whether ORs are adjusted, so coded per Amendment 1 rule (b): unadjusted, severity Unclear, Low confidence.

design_detail: Narrative review of valproic acid teratogenicity and counselling for women of reproductive age in psychiatry
population: Women of reproductive age treated with valproic acid for psychiatric disorders, including pregnant women
sample_size_detail: Narrative review; no sample size
rationale: Clinical overview with no systematic methods described; PubMed type Review.

design_detail: Prospective observational study of valproate-exposed term infants; incidence of neonatal hypoglycaemia and withdrawal, with crude correlations to maternal plasma valproate levels and dose
severity_measure: No adjustment; crude correlations of maternal valproate concentration/dose with infant outcomes; no epilepsy severity measures
comparison_group: None described in abstract (dose/concentration correlations within exposed infants)
population: Term infants of women with epilepsy treated with valproate during pregnancy (Denmark)
sample_size_detail: 22 infants (20 valproate monotherapy, 2 valproate plus carbamazepine); 13 hypoglycaemic, 10 with withdrawal symptoms
rationale: Prospective exposed-only cohort with descriptive risks and crude correlations; could alternatively be a case series or physiologic study, and the abstract's 'significantly elevated risk' implies an unstated comparator.

design_detail: Literature review with multi-database search (MEDLINE/PubMed, EMBASE, Scopus, Cochrane Library since 1996) of reports of gestational diabetes with second-generation antipsychotics; descriptive case counts with expert opinion, no pooling
population: Pregnant women exposed to second-generation antipsychotics
sample_size_detail: Number of included studies and pooled participants not reported; 18 GDM cases identified across reports
rationale: Describes a multi-database search with an inclusion rule (all articles on metabolic complications with specific SGAs), so coded systematic review. However, the expert-opinion format and PubMed 'Review' type make narrative review plausible.

design_detail: Retrospective cohort nested in US Medicaid Analytic eXtract (2000-2007); restriction to women with depression plus propensity-score stratification (100 strata); high-dimensional PS confirmatory analysis
severity_measure: Number of outpatient and inpatient depression diagnoses (depression severity proxies), plus other psychotropic medication use and other indications in the PS model
comparison_group: Women with depression not exposed to antidepressants in the first trimester (fully adjusted analysis); all unexposed women in unadjusted analysis
population: Pregnant women enrolled in US Medicaid (46 states + DC), 2000-2007, with liveborn infants
sample_size_detail: 949,504 eligible pregnancies; 64,389 exposed to any antidepressant in first trimester (46,144 SSRI) vs 885,115 unexposed. Fully adjusted depression-restricted SSRI analysis: 36,778 SSRI vs 180,564 unexposed
rationale: PS stratification within depression-restricted cohort explicitly controls 'proxies for depression severity' (counts of outpatient/inpatient depression diagnoses). No sibling analysis.

design_detail: Retrospective cohort in US Medicaid Analytic eXtract (2000-2007) restricted to women with depression; GEE log-binomial models with multivariable adjustment; hdPS and other sensitivity analyses
severity_measure: Number of outpatient (0, 1, 2-4, 5-9, >=10) and inpatient (0, 1, >=2) depression diagnoses, labelled depression-severity proxies; also anticonvulsant and benzodiazepine dispensing
comparison_group: Pregnant women with depression and no antidepressant exposure; SSRI monotherapy users in comparative-safety analysis
population: Pregnant women with depression diagnoses enrolled in US Medicaid, 2000-2007
sample_size_detail: 100,942 women with depression in cohort; 15,175 with first-trimester-only exposure excluded from primary analysis; Table 1 groups: 59,219 unexposed, 19,000 SSRI, 1,216 SNRI, 441 tricyclic, 2,622 bupropion, 647 other, 2,622 polytherapy
rationale: Models adjusted for 'depression-severity proxies' (counts of outpatient/inpatient depression diagnoses) within a depression-restricted cohort. Primary-analysis N derived from Table 1 group counts.

design_detail: Population-based prospective birth cohort using Finnish national registers (singleton live births 1996-2010); ORs comparing SSRI-exposed pregnancies with psychiatric-diagnosis unexposed and fully unexposed groups
severity_measure: Abstract-only; ORs reported but never stated whether adjusted (Amendment 1 rule b). Comparison by psychiatric diagnosis status (diagnosis alone does not count as severity)
comparison_group: Pregnancies unexposed to medications but with psychiatric diagnoses; and pregnancies unexposed to medications and without psychiatric diagnoses
population: Singleton live births in Finland, 1996-2010, and their mothers
sample_size_detail: Sampling frame 845,345 offspring; analytic groups 15,729 SSRI-exposed, 9,652 psychiatric diagnosis unexposed, 31,394 unexposed (sum 56,775)
rationale: Register-based non-randomized comparison 'accounting for psychiatric diagnoses' via comparison-group choice; abstract reports ORs but never says whether adjusted, so coded per Amendment 1 rule (b): unadjusted, severity Unclear, Low confidence.

design_detail: Systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis of neonatal outcomes and poor neonatal adaptation after in utero SRI antidepressant exposure
comparison_group: Unexposed infants, mostly infants of mothers diagnosed with depression
population: Neonates exposed in utero to serotonin reuptake inhibitor antidepressants
sample_size_detail: 33 studies (69 outcomes) included; 17 outcomes meta-analyzed; pooled participants not reported in abstract
rationale: PubMed Meta-Analysis/Systematic Review with 33 included studies. Component designs not stated explicitly but inferred observational from exposed vs unexposed infant comparisons.
